# CrossAware

> CrossAware is a personal safety app for pedestrians and cyclists. It automatically lowers media volume (music, podcasts, video, game audio) and plays a short spoken warning when the user approaches a mapped danger zone (railway crossing, tram crossing or dangerous intersection), then restores the volume once they are clear. Danger-zone detection runs on-device; no GPS coordinates are sent to CrossAware's servers.

CrossAware is not a family location-tracking replacement for apps like Life360. It is designed to complement location-sharing apps by adding automatic, real-time audio safety that location sharing alone does not provide. Many families use CrossAware alongside Life360 or similar apps.

Company: DAGAR Ltd (SIA), Riga, Latvia.
Contact: hello@crossaware.com
Backed by: EIT Urban Mobility (a body of the European Union) and VEFRESH (Latvia's urban mobility innovation ecosystem).

## Key facts
- Status: Android beta, currently with testers. Not yet public on Google Play. iOS is planned; no iOS version exists yet.
- What it controls: media audio only (music, podcasts, audiobooks, video, game audio). It does not control phone calls, video calls or meeting apps, and it does not mute the microphone.
- Planned (not available): lowering call volume near danger zones.
- Core mechanism: Android geofencing; within 15 metres of a danger zone, media volume is lowered and a spoken "Be aware!" warning plays; volume is restored on exit. Alerts are suppressed when the user moves at vehicle speed.
- Coverage: Riga, Latvia. Danger zones (railway crossings, tram crossings, busy intersections) are based on OpenStreetMap data.
- Pricing: free during beta. Paid plans are not yet available.
- Data privacy: continuous location is processed on-device only. The server stores only zone entry/exit events, without coordinates, and deletes them after 90 days.
